records.source: אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ עַל־דִּבְרֵ֖י הַבַּצָּרֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: [That] which came, [the] word of Yahweh, to Jeremiah concerning [the] matters of the droughts.
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that came to Jeremiah about the droughts:

L.1: That which came [as] the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to Jeremiah concerning the matters of the droughts:

R.1: This is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah about the droughts:

decisions.choice: a heading: "what came as the word of the LORD"
decisions.reason: The verse opens with "which", an unusual way to begin. It is a heading for what follows, a form Jeremiah uses again for some later oracles (46:1; 47:1; 49:34). It introduces the poems and dialogue of 14:2-15:9, which grow out of a time of drought.

decisions.choice: the droughts: times when the rain failed
decisions.reason: The noun means a lack of rain, a dry spell (17:8). It is plural here, which may point to repeated droughts or to one drought so long and severe that it is spoken of as many. "The matters of" means the events or circumstances of the drought; verses 2-6 describe them.

decisions.choice: That which came [as] the word of the LORD ... / The word of the LORD that came ... / This is the message the LORD gave Jeremiah ...
decisions.reason: The heading follows the wording settled for Jeremiah's formula "the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD", adjusted for this verse's different order. Readable says "message" as it does in that formula.

records.heading: The drought

records.source: אָבְלָ֣ה יְהוּדָ֔ה וּשְׁעָרֶ֥יהָ אֻמְלְל֖וּ קָדְר֣וּ לָאָ֑רֶץ וְצִוְחַ֥ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם עָלָֽתָה׃
records.gloss: Mourns Judah, and her gates languish; they are dark to the ground, and [the] cry of Jerusalem has gone up.
pieces: Judah mourns, \q her gates droop and fail; her people sit on the ground in black, \q and the cry of Jerusalem rises.

L.2: Judah mourns, \q and her gates languish; they are dark [in mourning] to the ground, \q and the cry of Jerusalem has gone up.

R.2: The people of Judah are in mourning. \q Their towns are wasting away; people sit on the ground in clothes of grief. \q A loud cry goes up from Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: her gates languish: the towns and the people who gather at their gates waste away
decisions.reason: The gate was the busy public place of a town, where people met, traded and held court. When its gates "languish" (the verb is used of plants that wither, Isaiah 24:7; Joel 1:10, 12), the whole life of the town is drying up (compare Isaiah 3:26, where Zion's gates mourn).

decisions.choice: dark to the ground: in dark mourning clothes, bowed down or sitting on the ground
decisions.reason: The verb means to be dark or dirty, and is used of mourners in dark, unwashed clothes (Psalms 35:14; 38:7; Job 30:28). "To the ground" adds the picture of mourners bowed low or sitting in the dust (Lamentations 2:10).

decisions.choice: cry: a loud scream of distress
decisions.reason: The word is a shrill outcry of people in trouble or grief (46:12; Isaiah 24:11). It "goes up" as if rising to heaven for help.

decisions.choice: her people sit on the ground in black / people sit on the ground in clothes of grief
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only that "they" are dark to the ground. Balanced and Readable name the people as the ones mourning and explain the darkness as mourning clothes (meaning decision m2). Readable says "towns" for the gates (m1).

records.source: וְאַדִּ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם שָׁלְח֥וּ צְעִירֵיהֶ֖ם לַמָּ֑יִם בָּ֣אוּ עַל־גֵּבִ֞ים לֹא־מָ֣צְאוּ מַ֗יִם שָׁ֤בוּ כְלֵיהֶם֙ רֵיקָ֔ם בֹּ֥שׁוּ וְהָכְלְמ֖וּ וְחָפ֥וּ רֹאשָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And their nobles have sent their young ones for water; they have come to cisterns, not have they found water, they have returned [with] their vessels empty; they are ashamed and humiliated, and have covered their head.
pieces: Their nobles send their young servants to fetch water; \q they reach the cisterns and there is no water; their vessels come back empty. \q They are ashamed and disgraced, and they cover their heads.

L.3: And their nobles send their young ones for water; \q they come to [the] cisterns, they find no water, they return [with] their vessels empty; \q they are ashamed and humiliated, and they cover their heads.

R.3: The leaders send their servants to get water. \q The servants go to the water pits, but there is no water. They come back with empty jars. \q They feel ashamed and disgraced, and they cover their heads.

decisions.choice: young ones: servants, the lowly members of the household
decisions.reason: The word means "little ones" or "young ones". Set beside "their nobles", it means the young or low-ranking servants sent out to do the work (48:4 uses the same word). The written text spells the word slightly differently from the form the scribes' margin says to read, with the same meaning; the reading form is followed here.

decisions.choice: cisterns: pits dug to hold rainwater
decisions.reason: The word names pits or hollows, often cut in rock, where rainwater collected (2 Kings 3:16; Isaiah 30:14). With no rain they stand empty. Jeremiah has already used empty, cracked cisterns as a picture of the people's false hopes (2:13).

decisions.choice: ashamed and humiliated ... cover their heads: signs of grief and disgrace
decisions.reason: "Ashamed" here is the shame of hopes that came to nothing: they went for water and came back with none. Covering the head was a sign of grief and humiliation (2 Samuel 15:30; Esther 6:12). The same words describe the farmers in verse 4.

decisions.choice: young servants / servants; cisterns / water pits; jars
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "servants" for the "young ones" (meaning decision m1). Readable calls the cisterns "water pits" and the vessels "jars", the usual containers for carrying water, and says "leaders" for the nobles.

records.source: בַּעֲב֤וּר הָאֲדָמָה֙ חַ֔תָּה כִּ֛י לֹא־הָיָ֥ה גֶ֖שֶׁם בָּאָ֑רֶץ בֹּ֥שׁוּ אִכָּרִ֖ים חָפ֥וּ רֹאשָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: Because of the ground [that] is shattered, for not there has been rain in the land, are ashamed [the] farmers, they have covered their head.
pieces: Because of the ground, cracked open \q since no rain has come on the land, \q the farmers are put to shame; they cover their heads.

L.4: Because of the ground that is cracked, \q for there has been no rain in the land, \q the farmers are ashamed; they cover their heads.

R.4: The ground has split open, \q since no rain has fallen on the land. \q The farmers are ashamed, and they cover their heads.

decisions.choice: cracked: shattered, broken up; the word is also used of people dismayed
decisions.reason: The verb means to be shattered, and it is often used of people broken by fear or dismay (1:17; 8:9). Said of the ground, it pictures dry earth split open, and it may also hint that the land itself is dismayed, as Judah and its gates mourn in verse 2.

decisions.choice: farmers ashamed: their hopes for a harvest have failed
decisions.reason: The farmers are the men who plowed and worked the fields. They are "ashamed" in the same way as the water carriers of verse 3: they did their work, and the rain they counted on never came. They cover their heads as those in verse 3 do.

decisions.choice: The ground has split open, since no rain has fallen
decisions.reason: Readable makes "because of the ground" into a sentence of its own and lets the farmers' shame follow from it, keeping the sentence short.

records.source: כִּ֤י גַם־אַיֶּ֨לֶת֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה יָלְדָ֖ה וְעָז֑וֹב כִּ֥י לֹֽא־הָיָ֖ה דֶּֽשֶׁא׃
records.gloss: For even [the] doe in the field has given birth and abandoned, for not there is grass.
pieces: Even the doe in the open field gives birth and then leaves her young behind, \q because there is no grass.

L.5: For even the doe in the field gives birth and abandons [her young], \q for there is no grass.

R.5: Even a mother deer gives birth in the field and then leaves her baby, \q because there is no grass.

decisions.choice: gives birth and abandons: the second verb continues the first; the newborn is the one left
decisions.reason: The second verb is in a form (the infinitive) that carries on the action of the first: she gives birth and then leaves. No object is stated, but the one abandoned is the newborn.

decisions.choice: the doe: a mother animal that would not leave her young unless forced to
decisions.reason: The doe was a picture of gentleness and of tender care for its young (Proverbs 5:19; Job 39:1-4). That she leaves her newborn fawn to die shows how desperate the drought has become: even the strongest instinct of a mother fails when there is nothing to eat.

decisions.choice: [her young] / her young / her baby
decisions.reason: The object of "abandons" is supplied at every level (in brackets at Literal), since English needs one and the context makes it plain (meaning decision m1).

records.source: וּפְרָאִים֙ עָמְד֣וּ עַל־שְׁפָיִ֔ם שָׁאֲפ֥וּ ר֖וּחַ כַּתַּנִּ֑ים כָּל֥וּ עֵינֵיהֶ֖ם כִּי־אֵ֥ין עֵֽשֶׂב׃
records.gloss: And wild donkeys have stood on bare heights, they have panted [for] air like jackals; have failed their eyes, for there is no vegetation.
pieces: Wild donkeys stand on the bare heights, \q gasping for air like jackals; \q their eyes grow dim, because there are no plants.

L.6: And wild donkeys stand on the bare heights; \q they pant for air like jackals; \q their eyes fail, for there is no vegetation.

R.6: Wild donkeys stand on bare hilltops, \q gasping for breath like jackals. \q Their eyes grow weak, because nothing green is growing.

decisions.choice: bare heights: open, treeless hills
decisions.reason: The word names high, bare places with no trees (3:2, 21; 4:11; Isaiah 41:18). The wild donkeys, animals of the open country (2:24; Job 39:5-8), go up to them in search of wind or water.

decisions.choice: pant for air like jackals: gasp open-mouthed, sniffing the wind
decisions.reason: The verb means to gasp or pant, or to sniff eagerly at the air (2:24 uses it of a wild donkey sniffing the wind). Jackals were known as animals of waste places that howl and pant (9:10; 10:22). Here the donkeys stand with mouths open, weak from thirst.

decisions.choice: their eyes fail: they grow dim from weakness and from looking in vain
decisions.reason: Eyes that "fail" or "are spent" are eyes dimmed by hunger, weakness or long waiting for help that does not come (Lamentations 4:17; Psalms 69:4).

decisions.choice: nothing green is growing
decisions.reason: Readable explains "vegetation" in plain words: no green plants are growing for the animals to eat.

records.source: אִם־עֲוֺנֵ֨ינוּ֙ עָ֣נוּ בָ֔נוּ יְהוָ֕ה עֲשֵׂ֖ה לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמֶ֑ךָ כִּֽי־רַבּ֥וּ מְשׁוּבֹתֵ֖ינוּ לְךָ֥ חָטָֽאנוּ׃
records.gloss: Though our iniquities have testified against us, Yahweh, act for the sake of your name; for many are our turnings away, against you we have sinned.
pieces: Even though our sins bear witness against us, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q act for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name; \q for we have turned away many times; we have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.7: Though our iniquities testify against us, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q act for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name; \q for our turnings away are many; against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} we have sinned.

R.7: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, our sins speak against us. \q But act to help us, for the honor of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. \q We have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} again and again. We have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: a new voice: the people pray to the LORD
decisions.reason: After the picture of the drought (verses 2-6), the people (or the prophet speaking for them) turn to God in prayer (verses 7-9). The LORD answers in verse 10. A second prayer follows in verses 19-22.

decisions.choice: our iniquities testify against us: our sins stand as witnesses in court
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a witness giving evidence (Numbers 35:30; Isaiah 59:12). The people admit that their own wrongs speak against them before God; they do not plead innocence.

decisions.choice: for the sake of your name: the plea rests on who God is, not on the people's merit
decisions.reason: God's name is his reputation and character as he has made himself known. Since the people have no right to help, they appeal to God's own honor and faithfulness (verse 21; Psalms 25:11; 79:9; Ezekiel 20:9).

decisions.choice: turnings away: acts of unfaithfulness, falling away from God
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "turn" or "return" and means turning away from God. Jeremiah uses it for Israel's repeated unfaithfulness (2:19; 3:22; 5:6), playing on God's call to "return".

decisions.choice: sins (for iniquities); act to help us, for the honor of your name
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "sins" for the word rendered "iniquities" at Literal, as in Isaiah. Readable says what the act is ("to help us") and explains "for the sake of your name" as "for the honor of your name" (meaning decision m3).

records.source: מִקְוֵה֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מֽוֹשִׁיע֖וֹ בְּעֵ֣ת צָרָ֑ה לָ֤מָּה תִֽהְיֶה֙ כְּגֵ֣ר בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּכְאֹרֵ֖חַ נָטָ֥ה לָלֽוּן׃
records.gloss: Hope of Israel, its savior in a time of distress, why should you be like a sojourner in the land, and like a traveler [who] has turned aside to spend the night?
pieces: Hope of Israel, who saves it in a time of trouble, \q why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} seem an outsider in the land, \q a traveler who turns aside to camp for one night?

L.8: Hope of Israel, its savior in a time of distress, \q why should {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be like a sojourner in the land, \q and like a traveler who turns aside to spend the night?

R.8: Israel hopes in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save them in times of trouble. \q So why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} act like a stranger in this land, \q like someone passing through who only stops to sleep?

decisions.choice: Hope of Israel: the one Israel waits for and trusts
decisions.reason: The noun means hope or the object of hope. Jeremiah uses the title again (17:13; compare 50:7), where it stands beside "the spring of living water". The noun can also mean a pool of water, a fitting double sense in a prayer for rain.

decisions.choice: a sojourner ... a traveler: people with no lasting stake in the land
decisions.reason: A sojourner was a foreigner living in a land not his own, and a traveler stopped only for a night on his way somewhere else. The people complain that God, who should be at home among them, acts as if their land and its trouble were no concern of his. The verb "turns aside" may also mean "pitches [a tent]".

decisions.choice: why should you be: a complaint, not a request for information
decisions.reason: The question is a lament, like those in the psalms (Psalms 10:1; 22:2). It protests that God's apparent absence does not fit who he is.

decisions.choice: outsider (Balanced); stranger (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word rendered "sojourner" at Literal is "outsider" at Balanced and "stranger" at Readable, the wording used for it in 22:3 and since Leviticus; both suit the picture of someone not at home in the land.

decisions.choice: Israel hopes in you; you save them
decisions.reason: Readable turns the two titles of God into statements, so that the address is clear before the question.

records.source: לָ֤מָּה תִֽהְיֶה֙ כְּאִ֣ישׁ נִדְהָ֔ם כְּגִבּ֖וֹר לֹא־יוּכַ֣ל לְהוֹשִׁ֑יעַ וְאַתָּ֧ה בְקִרְבֵּ֣נוּ יְהוָ֗ה וְשִׁמְךָ֛ עָלֵ֥ינוּ נִקְרָ֖א אַל־תַּנִּחֵֽנוּ׃ס
records.gloss: Why should you be like a man confounded, like a warrior [who] not is able to save? And you [are] in our midst, Yahweh, and your name over us is called; do not leave us.
pieces: Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} like someone stunned, \q like a soldier who cannot save anyone? \q Yet {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are among us, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name is spoken over us; do not abandon us.

L.9: Why should {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be like a man taken by surprise, \q like a warrior who is not able to save? \q Yet {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are in our midst, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name is called over us; do not leave us.

R.9: Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} like a man who does not know what to do, \q like a fighter who cannot rescue anyone? \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are here with us, and we belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Do not leave us!

decisions.choice: taken by surprise: stunned, at a loss, unable to act
decisions.reason: The verb occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible. Related words suggest being dismayed or caught off guard, someone so startled he cannot act. The picture is of a strong man who stands helpless.

decisions.choice: your name is called over us: we belong to you
decisions.reason: To have someone's name called over a thing or a people means they belong to him (7:10; 15:16; Deuteronomy 28:10; 2 Samuel 12:28). The people remind God that they are his own, so their shame is his.

decisions.choice: leave us: let us go, set us down and walk away
decisions.reason: The verb means to set down or leave something lying. The people ask God not to drop them and walk away, which is what the stranger and the traveler of verse 8 would do.

decisions.choice: we belong to you
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom of God's name called over the people (meaning decision m2).

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה כֵּ֤ן אָֽהֲבוּ֙ לָנ֔וּעַ רַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם לֹ֣א חָשָׂ֑כוּ וַיהוָה֙ לֹ֣א רָצָ֔ם עַתָּה֙ יִזְכֹּ֣ר עֲוֺנָ֔ם וְיִפְקֹ֖ד חַטֹּאתָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh to this people: so they have loved to wander, their feet not they have held back; and Yahweh not has accepted them; now he will remember their iniquity and punish their sins.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this about this people: They love to wander; \q they do not keep their feet in check. \q So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} takes no pleasure in them; \q now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will remember their guilt and punish their sins.

L.10: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning this people: So they have loved to wander; \q they have not held back their feet. \q And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does not accept them; \q now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will remember their iniquity and punish their sins.

R.10: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says about these people: They love to wander off. \q They do not hold themselves back. \q That is why {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} takes no pleasure in them. \q Now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will remember the wrong they have done and make them pay for their sins.

decisions.choice: so they have loved to wander: the LORD answers the prayer by describing the people
decisions.reason: "So" (or "truly") sums up the people's ways: they pray for God to stay, yet they love to roam from him. The verb "wander" is used of people going restlessly from place to place (Amos 4:8); here it means running after other gods and other helpers (2:23-25, 36).

decisions.choice: the LORD does not accept them ... he will remember: God speaks of himself by name
decisions.reason: The LORD's answer speaks of "the LORD" and "he" rather than "I", like a judge announcing a verdict. The word "accept" is used of God accepting an offering with favor (Leviticus 1:4; Amos 5:22), and it prepares for verse 12.

decisions.choice: now he will remember their iniquity and punish their sins: the same words as Hosea 8:13
decisions.reason: The second half of the verse repeats Hosea 8:13 word for word, where it is said of Israel's sacrifices. Jeremiah applies to Judah what Hosea said of the northern kingdom a century before.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD: no quotation marks
decisions.reason: As in the rest of Jeremiah's poetry, the LORD's words after the formula are given without quotation marks.

decisions.choice: make them pay for their sins
decisions.reason: Readable puts "punish their sins" as "make them pay for their sins". It says "the wrong they have done" for "iniquity" to avoid saying "sins" twice.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י אַל־תִּתְפַּלֵּ֛ל בְּעַד־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה לְטוֹבָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me: do not pray for this people for good.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Do not pray for the good of this people.

L.11: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Do not pray for this people for [their] good.

R.11: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Do not pray for good things to happen to these people.

decisions.choice: do not pray for this people: the command again
decisions.reason: The LORD has already told Jeremiah not to plead for the people (7:16; 11:14), and he will say it once more in 15:1, where even Moses and Samuel would not be heard. A prophet was expected to pray for the people (1 Samuel 12:23); being forbidden to do so shows that judgment is now certain.

decisions.choice: for good: for their welfare, for things to go well with them
decisions.reason: "Good" here means well-being and prosperity, the opposite of the disaster that is coming (21:10; 24:6; 39:16).

decisions.choice: a prose dialogue begins
decisions.reason: Verses 11-16 are a conversation in prose between the LORD and Jeremiah. The LORD's words that begin here run to the end of verse 12; his second answer runs from verse 14 to the end of verse 18.

decisions.choice: quotation marks for the prose dialogue
decisions.reason: The dialogue of verses 11-18 is prose narrative, so its speech takes quotation marks, unlike the poetry around it.

records.heading: Prophets who promise peace

records.source: כִּ֣י יָצֻ֗מוּ אֵינֶ֤נִּי שֹׁמֵ֨עַ֙ אֶל־רִנָּתָ֔ם וְכִ֧י יַעֲל֛וּ עֹלָ֥ה וּמִנְחָ֖ה אֵינֶ֣נִּי רֹצָ֑ם כִּ֗י בַּחֶ֨רֶב֙ וּבָרָעָ֣ב וּבַדֶּ֔בֶר אָנֹכִ֖י מְכַלֶּ֥ה אוֹתָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: When they fast, not I [am] listening to their cry; and when they offer up burnt offering and grain offering, not I [am] accepting them; for by the sword and by the famine and by the pestilence I [am] finishing them.
pieces: When they fast, I will not hear their cry; when they present burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will take no pleasure in them. No, I am going to put an end to them by sword, famine and plague."

L.12: When they fast, I am not listening to their cry; and when they offer up burnt offering and grain offering, I am not accepting them; but by sword, by famine and by pestilence I am going to finish them off."

R.12: They may go without food, but I will not listen to their cries. They may bring burnt offerings and grain offerings, but I will not accept them. I am going to destroy them by war, famine and disease."

decisions.choice: fasting and offerings: the usual ways of seeking God's help in a disaster
decisions.reason: In a drought or other crisis the people fasted and offered sacrifices to plead for help (Joel 1:13-14; 2:12-17; 36:9). The LORD refuses them because the worship is not matched by changed lives (7:21-23; Isaiah 1:11-15).

decisions.choice: cry: a loud call or ringing shout, here a plea for help
decisions.reason: The word can be a shout of joy or of prayer (7:16; 11:14 use it of pleading). Here it is the people's loud prayer for rescue.

decisions.choice: sword, famine and pestilence: the disasters of war and siege
decisions.reason: The three come together when an enemy besieges a city: death in battle, starvation, and the disease that spreads among the hungry. Jeremiah names them together often (21:7, 9; 24:10; 27:8; 29:17-18). The word for the third means a deadly epidemic.

decisions.choice: I am going to finish them: an action that is about to happen
decisions.reason: The participle presents the destruction as already under way or about to come. The verb means to bring to an end, to finish off.

decisions.choice: sword, famine and plague / war, famine and disease; go without food
decisions.reason: The three disasters follow the wording settled for Jeremiah. Readable explains fasting as going without food.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֞ר אֲהָ֣הּ׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה הַנְּבִאִ֜ים אֹמְרִ֤ים לָהֶם֙ לֹֽא־תִרְא֣וּ חֶ֔רֶב וְרָעָ֖ב לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־שְׁל֤וֹם אֱמֶת֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן לָכֶ֔ם בַּמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And I said: Alas, Lord Yahweh! Look, the prophets [are] saying to them, not you will see sword, and famine not will be to you; for peace of truth I will give to you in this place.
pieces: Then I said, "Oh, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! Look, the prophets tell them, 'The sword you will not see, and famine will not come on you; instead I will give you peace that is sure, here in this place.'"

L.13: And I said, "Ah, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! Look, the prophets are saying to them, 'You will not see [the] sword, and famine will not come to you, but true peace I will give you in this place.'"

R.13: But I said, "Oh no, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! The prophets keep saying to the people, 'You will not face war or famine. I will give you real peace that lasts, here in this place.'"

decisions.choice: Ah: a cry of dismay
decisions.reason: Jeremiah uses this cry when he is distressed and protests to God (1:6; 4:10; 32:17). Here he pleads that the people have been misled by their prophets.

decisions.choice: true peace: peace that is real and lasting
decisions.reason: The word joined to "peace" means truth, reliability, firmness. The prophets promise a peace that can be counted on to last, the very thing God says is not coming (6:14; 8:11).

decisions.choice: I will give: the prophets speak in God's name
decisions.reason: The prophets speak as if God himself were saying "I will give". "This place" is Jerusalem and its temple (7:3, 7). Jeremiah reports their message to show where the people's false confidence came from; God answers in verses 14-16.

decisions.choice: keep saying
decisions.reason: The Hebrew participle describes something the prophets were doing at the time and kept doing. Readable makes the continuing action plain with "keep saying" and names "the people" for "them".

decisions.choice: real peace that lasts
decisions.reason: Readable uses two words for the one Hebrew word joined to "peace" (meaning decision m2).

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י שֶׁ֚קֶר הַנְּבִאִים֙ נִבְּאִ֣ים בִּשְׁמִ֔י לֹ֤א שְׁלַחְתִּים֙ וְלֹ֣א צִוִּיתִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א דִבַּ֖רְתִּי אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם חֲז֨וֹן שֶׁ֜קֶר וְקֶ֤סֶם וֶֽאֱלִיל֙ וְתַרְמִ֣ית לִבָּ֔ם הֵ֖מָּה מִֽתְנַבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me: falsehood the prophets [are] prophesying in my name; not I sent them, and not I commanded them, and not I spoke to them; a vision of falsehood and divination and worthlessness and [the] deceit of their heart they [are] prophesying to you.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Lies are what the prophets prophesy in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. I did not send them, I gave them no command, and I did not speak to them. What they prophesy to you is a false vision, divination, worthless things and the deceit of their own hearts.

L.14: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Falsehood the prophets are prophesying in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. I did not send them, and I did not command them, and I did not speak to them. A false vision and divination and worthlessness and the deceit of their [own] heart they are prophesying to you.

R.14: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "The prophets are telling lies and saying they speak for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I did not send them. I did not give them orders, and I did not speak to them. The visions they tell you about are false. They try to tell the future by magic, which is worthless. They make things up in their own minds and tell them to you.

decisions.choice: worthlessness ... deceit: the forms the scribes' margin says to read
decisions.reason: For these two words the written Hebrew text has slightly different spellings from the forms the scribes noted in the margin to be read aloud. The meaning is the same either way; the reading form is followed here.

decisions.choice: divination: trying to learn the future by signs and omens
decisions.reason: Divination meant reading omens, for example by casting lots or examining livers, to discover hidden things. The law forbade it in Israel (Deuteronomy 18:10, 14), so to prophesy by it was to stand outside God's way of speaking.

decisions.choice: worthlessness: something empty, of no use
decisions.reason: The word means nothing, a thing of no worth (Job 13:4). It is often used of idols, the "worthless" gods (Isaiah 2:8; Leviticus 19:4). Here it describes what the prophets say: empty words with nothing behind them.

decisions.choice: the deceit of their heart: self-deception; ideas that come from their own minds
decisions.reason: The heart is the place of thinking and planning. Their message comes from their own minds, not from God (23:16, 26). The phrase can mean both that they invent it and that they themselves are deceived.

decisions.choice: saying they speak for me; tell the future by magic; make things up in their own minds
decisions.reason: Readable explains "in my name", "divination" and "the deceit of their heart" in plain words, and breaks the list into short sentences.

records.source: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה עַֽל־הַנְּבִאִ֞ים הַנִּבְּאִ֣ים בִּשְׁמִי֮ וַאֲנִ֣י לֹֽא־שְׁלַחְתִּים֒ וְהֵ֨מָּה֙ אֹֽמְרִ֔ים חֶ֣רֶב וְרָעָ֔ב לֹ֥א יִהְיֶ֖ה בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את בַּחֶ֤רֶב וּבָֽרָעָב֙ יִתַּ֔מּוּ הַנְּבִאִ֖ים הָהֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh concerning the prophets who [are] prophesying in my name, and I not sent them, and they [are] saying, sword and famine not will be in this land: by the sword and by the famine will come to an end the prophets those.
pieces: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this about the prophets who prophesy in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name although I did not send them, and who say, 'Sword and famine will not come on this land': Those prophets will come to their end by sword and famine.

L.15: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning the prophets who are prophesying in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, though I did not send them, and who are saying, 'Sword and famine will not be in this land': By sword and by famine those prophets will come to their end.

R.15: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says about the prophets who claim to speak for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, though I did not send them. They say, 'No war or famine will come to this land.' But those prophets will die by war and famine.

decisions.choice: by sword and famine: the prophets will die by the very things they said would not come
decisions.reason: The punishment matches the lie: those who denied that sword and famine would come will be the first to fall to them. The same words that open their false promise close the verdict on them.

decisions.choice: says the LORD ... my name ... I did not send them: God speaks of himself in both ways
decisions.reason: The verse begins with the formula "thus says the LORD" and then has God speak as "I" within the same sentence, as prophetic speech often does.

decisions.choice: come to their end: be finished off, perish
decisions.reason: The verb means to be complete or finished. Of people it means to die out completely (24:10; 44:12, 18).

decisions.choice: claim to speak for me; die
decisions.reason: Readable explains "prophesying in my name" and says plainly that the prophets will die. It breaks the long sentence into three.

records.source: וְהָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֣מָּה נִבְּאִ֣ים לָהֶ֡ם יִֽהְי֣וּ מֻשְׁלָכִים֩ בְּחֻצ֨וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם מִפְּנֵ֣י׀הָרָעָ֣ב וְהַחֶ֗רֶב וְאֵ֤ין מְקַבֵּר֙ לָהֵ֔מָּה הֵ֣מָּה נְשֵׁיהֶ֔ם וּבְנֵיהֶ֖ם וּבְנֹֽתֵיהֶ֑ם וְשָׁפַכְתִּ֥י עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם אֶת־רָעָתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And the people to whom they [are] prophesying to them will be thrown out in [the] streets of Jerusalem because of the famine and the sword, and there [will be] none burying them, them, their wives and their sons and their daughters; and I will pour out on them their evil.
pieces: The people who hear their prophecies will be flung into the streets of Jerusalem by famine and sword, and no one will bury them, nor their wives, their sons and their daughters. I will pour their own evil out upon them.

L.16: And the people to whom they are prophesying will be thrown out into the streets of Jerusalem because of the famine and the sword, with no one to bury them, them, their wives and their sons and their daughters; and I will pour out on them their evil.

R.16: The people who listen to them will lie dead in the streets of Jerusalem, killed by famine and war. No one will be there to bury them, their wives, their sons or their daughters. I will pour out on them the trouble their own evil has earned.

decisions.choice: thrown out with no one to bury them: the worst disgrace
decisions.reason: To lie unburied was the greatest shame and a sign of God's curse (7:33; 8:1-2; 16:4; Deuteronomy 28:26). Here so many die, or so few are left, that no one buries them.

decisions.choice: the people who listen share the prophets' fate
decisions.reason: The people are not excused because they were misled: they chose to believe the prophets who told them what they wanted to hear (5:31).

decisions.choice: their evil: both their wickedness and the disaster it brings
decisions.reason: The word means evil, and it can mean both wrongdoing and the harm that follows. God will pour out on them the result of their own wickedness: the disaster is their evil come back on their heads (2:19; 6:19).

decisions.choice: their own evil / the trouble their own evil has earned
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "own" to show that the evil is theirs. Readable spells out both senses of the word (meaning decision m3).

records.source: וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֲלֵיהֶם֙ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה תֵּרַ֨דְנָה עֵינַ֥י דִּמְעָ֛ה לַ֥יְלָה וְיוֹמָ֖ם וְאַל־תִּדְמֶ֑ינָה כִּי֩ שֶׁ֨בֶר גָּד֜וֹל נִשְׁבְּרָ֗ה בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת־עַמִּ֔י מַכָּ֖ה נַחְלָ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And you will say to them this word: let run down my eyes [with] tears night and day, and let them not cease; for [with] a great breaking is broken [the] virgin daughter of my people, [with] a wound very sick.
pieces: Say this word to them: \q 'Let tears stream from my eyes night and day, and let them not stop, \q for the virgin, my dear people, has been broken by a great blow, \q a wound that is very severe.

L.17: And you shall say to them this word: \q 'Let my eyes run down with tears night and day, and let them not cease, \q for the virgin daughter of my people is broken with a great breaking, \q with a very grievous wound.

R.17: Tell them this: \q 'Let my eyes pour out tears night and day; let them never stop. \q My people, my precious young daughter, have been crushed by a terrible blow, \q a wound that is very serious.

decisions.choice: the prophet's lament, given as the LORD's word: my eyes ... my people
decisions.reason: The LORD tells Jeremiah to say "this word", and what follows is a lament for the people in the first person. The weeping is Jeremiah's (compare 8:23; 13:17), but because it is spoken as the LORD's word it also carries God's own grief over his people (9:9). Verses 17-18 belong to the LORD's speech that began in verse 14.

decisions.choice: the virgin daughter of my people: the nation pictured as a young unmarried woman
decisions.reason: "Daughter of my people" pictures the whole people as a beloved daughter, and "virgin" adds youth and the shame of violation (compare "virgin daughter of Zion", Isaiah 37:22). The phrase expresses tender love and grief together (8:21-23).

decisions.choice: broken with a great breaking ... a very grievous wound: a deep wound, like a broken bone
decisions.reason: The noun and verb are both from the word for breaking, used of a fracture or a crushing disaster (4:6; 6:1, 14; 8:21). The last phrase is a wound that is sick, one that will not heal (10:19; 30:12).

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for the word Jeremiah is to say
decisions.reason: The lament of verses 17-18 is the "word" the LORD gives Jeremiah to say, inside the LORD's speech of verses 14-18, so it takes single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: the virgin, my dear people / my people, my precious young daughter
decisions.reason: Following the wording settled for Jeremiah, Balanced says "my dear people" for "the daughter of my people" and keeps "virgin". Readable says "my people" and keeps the picture of a young daughter (meaning decision m2).

records.source: אִם־יָצָ֣אתִי הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה וְהִנֵּה֙ חַלְלֵי־חֶ֔רֶב וְאִם֙ בָּ֣אתִי הָעִ֔יר וְהִנֵּ֖ה תַּחֲלוּאֵ֣י רָעָ֑ב כִּֽי־גַם־נָבִ֧יא גַם־כֹּהֵ֛ן סָחֲר֥וּ אֶל־אֶ֖רֶץ וְלֹ֥א יָדָֽעוּ׃ס
records.gloss: If I have gone out [to] the field, then look, [the] slain of [the] sword; and if I have entered the city, then look, [the] sicknesses of famine; for both prophet and priest have gone about to a land, and not they know.
pieces: If I go out to the open fields, there lie those slain by the sword; \q if I enter the city, \q there are those sick from famine. \q Even prophet and priest go roaming off to a land they do not know.'"

L.18: If I go out into the field, look, those slain by the sword! \q And if I enter the city, \q look, the sicknesses of famine! \q For both prophet and priest go about to a land they do not know.'"

R.18: When I go out into the fields, I see people killed in war. \q When I go into the city, \q I see people sick from the famine. \q Even the prophets and priests are wandering off to a land they do not know.'"

decisions.choice: look: the speaker sees the dead with his own eyes
decisions.reason: Each "if" is followed by "look", as if the prophet were already seeing what will happen. Outside the walls the enemy's sword kills; inside them famine does.

decisions.choice: go about to a land they do not know: go off into a land they do not know, that is, into exile
alternatives: wander through the land with no understanding
carry on their business in the land and know nothing
decisions.reason: The verb means to go about, often as a trader travels from place to place. With "to a land" it most likely means that prophet and priest are taken off to a foreign land they have never known (15:14; 16:13; 17:4). It may instead mean that they go about the land in confusion, not knowing what to do, or that they carry on their trade in the land without real knowledge of God.

decisions.choice: the sicknesses of famine: people wasting away from hunger
decisions.reason: The word means diseases or sufferings. Joined to "famine" it means the sickness of people starving inside the besieged city.

decisions.choice: there lie ... there are / I see
decisions.reason: For "look" Balanced points to what lies there and Readable says "I see". Readable says "killed in war" for "slain by the sword", as it says "war" for the sword elsewhere in Jeremiah.

records.source: הֲמָאֹ֨ס מָאַ֜סְתָּ אֶת־יְהוּדָ֗ה אִם־בְּצִיּוֹן֙ גָּעֲלָ֣ה נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ מַדּ֨וּעַ֙ הִכִּיתָ֔נוּ וְאֵ֥ין לָ֖נוּ מַרְפֵּ֑א קַוֵּ֤ה לְשָׁלוֹם֙ וְאֵ֣ין ט֔וֹב וּלְעֵ֥ת מַרְפֵּ֖א וְהִנֵּ֥ה בְעָתָֽה׃
records.gloss: Utterly have you rejected Judah? Or Zion has your soul loathed? Why have you struck us, and there is not for us healing? Hoping for peace, and there is no good, and for a time of healing, and look, terror.
pieces: Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rejected Judah altogether? \q Has Zion become hateful to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}? \q Why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} struck us down beyond any healing? \q We hoped for peace, but nothing good came; \q for a time of healing, but there was only terror.

L.19: Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} utterly rejected Judah? \q Has {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} soul loathed Zion? \q Why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} struck us, and there is no healing for us? \q Hoping for peace, but no good [came]; \q and for a time of healing, and look, terror.

R.19: Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} turned away from Judah for good? \q Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hate the people of Zion? \q Why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hurt us so badly that we cannot get well? \q We hoped for peace, but nothing good happened. \q We hoped for a time of healing, but now there is only terror.

decisions.choice: utterly rejected: the verb is doubled for force
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated in the Hebrew ("rejecting, have you rejected") to make it strong: have you rejected Judah completely and for good? Lamentations 5:22 asks the same question in the same words.

decisions.choice: the people pray again
decisions.reason: As in verses 7-9, the people (or the prophet on their behalf) speak to God. This second prayer runs to verse 22.

decisions.choice: your soul: your very self
decisions.reason: The soul here is the whole inner self, with its desires and feelings. To ask whether God's soul loathes Zion is to ask whether he has turned against her with all that he is (compare Leviticus 26:11, 30, where God promises that his soul will not loathe his people).

decisions.choice: hoping for peace ... terror: the same words as 8:15
decisions.reason: The second half of the verse repeats 8:15 almost exactly, and each level words it as there; the only difference is that here the Hebrew joins the last line with "and". The people now take up the words of the earlier lament as their own complaint.

decisions.choice: the people of Zion
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Zion" for the name Zion, which here stands for Jerusalem and those who live there.

records.heading: Have you rejected Judah?

records.source: יָדַ֧עְנוּ יְהוָ֛ה רִשְׁעֵ֖נוּ עֲוֺ֣ן אֲבוֹתֵ֑ינוּ כִּ֥י חָטָ֖אנוּ לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: We know, Yahweh, our wickedness, [the] iniquity of our fathers; for we have sinned against you.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, we know our wickedness and the guilt of our ancestors; \q we have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.20: We know, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, our wickedness, the iniquity of our fathers, \q for we have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.20: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, we admit the evil we have done and the sins of our ancestors. \q We have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: we know: we acknowledge, we confess
decisions.reason: "Know" here means to recognize and admit openly. It answers the charge that the people did not know (2:8; 9:2, 5) with a confession (3:13).

decisions.choice: the iniquity of our fathers: the people confess the sins of their ancestors along with their own
decisions.reason: Confession in Israel often joined the sins of past generations to the present one (Leviticus 26:40; Nehemiah 9:2; Psalms 106:6; Daniel 9:8). The people own the whole history of unfaithfulness that has brought judgment (3:25; 11:10).

decisions.choice: the guilt of our ancestors / the sins of our ancestors
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" for "fathers", since the word means the earlier generations, and use "guilt" and "sins" for "iniquity", as in Isaiah.

records.source: אַל־תִּנְאַץ֙ לְמַ֣עַן שִׁמְךָ֔ אַל־תְּנַבֵּ֖ל כִּסֵּ֣א כְבוֹדֶ֑ךָ זְכֹ֕ר אַל־תָּפֵ֥ר בְּרִֽיתְךָ֖ אִתָּֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: Do not spurn, for the sake of your name; do not disgrace [the] throne of your glory; remember, do not break your covenant with us.
pieces: Do not treat us with scorn, for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name; \q do not bring shame on the throne of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory. \q Remember, and do not break {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant with us.

L.21: Do not spurn [us], for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name; \q do not disgrace the throne of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory; \q remember, do not break {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant with us.

R.21: Do not turn from us in disgust; think of the honor of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. \q Do not let shame come to the throne of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory. \q Please remember! Do not break {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant with us.

decisions.choice: do not spurn: the object, "us", is understood
decisions.reason: The verb, to treat with contempt, has no object in the Hebrew, but the context makes clear that the people are asking God not to reject them.

decisions.choice: the throne of your glory: Jerusalem and its temple, where God was said to be enthroned
decisions.reason: Jeremiah calls Jerusalem "the throne of the LORD" (3:17) and the temple "a glorious throne" (17:12). If the city falls, it will look to the nations as if Israel's God could not protect his own throne, which is why the people appeal to his honor.

decisions.choice: remember, do not break: two commands side by side
decisions.reason: "Remember" stands on its own, with no object: remember us, or remember your covenant. The second command, "do not break your covenant with us", says what remembering would mean. The people appeal to God's promise not to break his covenant even when Israel is punished (Leviticus 26:44-45; Judges 2:1).

decisions.choice: treat us with scorn / turn from us in disgust; think of the honor of your name
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "us" as the object (meaning decision m1). Readable explains "for the sake of your name" and adds "Please" to show the tone of a plea.

records.source: הֲיֵ֨שׁ בְּהַבְלֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ מַגְשִׁמִ֔ים וְאִם־הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם יִתְּנ֣וּ רְבִבִ֑ים הֲלֹ֨א אַתָּה־ה֜וּא יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ וּ֨נְקַוֶּה־לָּ֔ךְ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה עָשִׂ֖יתָ אֶת־כָּל־אֵֽלֶּה׃פ
records.gloss: Are there among [the] vanities of the nations [ones] bringing rain? Or the heavens, will they give showers? [Is it] not you, he, Yahweh our God? And we hope for you, for you have made all these.
pieces: Is there any among the empty idols of the nations that can make it rain? \q Can the heavens give showers on their own? \q Is it not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God? We wait in hope for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q for it is {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who made all these things.

L.22: Are there among the worthless [idols] of the nations [any] who bring rain? \q Or can the heavens give showers? \q Is it not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God? We hope in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made all these [things].

R.22: Not one of the useless idols of the nations can send rain. \q The sky cannot pour down showers on its own. \q Only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God. So we look to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with hope, \q because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made all these things.

decisions.choice: worthless idols: literally "vapors", things with no substance
decisions.reason: The word means a breath or vapor, something that vanishes. Jeremiah uses it for idols, which have no power at all (8:19; 10:8, 15; Deuteronomy 32:21).

decisions.choice: only the LORD gives rain
decisions.reason: The nations looked to gods such as Baal to send rain, and Israel had followed them (2:8; Hosea 2:7-10). The prayer confesses that neither idols nor the sky itself can send rain; it comes from the LORD alone (5:24; 10:13; Deuteronomy 11:14; 1 Kings 18).

decisions.choice: is it not you: "you are he", you are the one
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "are not you he", meaning "are you not the one who does this?" It is a question that expects the answer yes.

decisions.choice: made all these: the heavens, the rain and the showers
alternatives: you have done all these things
decisions.reason: "All these" most likely means the things just named: the heavens and the rain they give. God made them and governs them. It may also mean that God has done all these things, including holding back the rain as judgment.

decisions.choice: statements in place of questions
decisions.reason: The three questions expect clear answers (no, no, and yes). Readable gives the answers as statements so that the meaning is plain. Balanced and Readable add "on their own" to the second question, which is about whether the sky can send rain without God.
